text: Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move relating (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-001 Keying, declared adapted (Goffman, E. (1974) Frame Analysis; Bateson, G. (1972) A theory of play and fantasy; recalled); 10 third-order themes: T3-001, T3-023, T3-032, T3-048, T3-064, T3-093, T3-095, T3-097, T3-100, T3-106. Why: the April Fools themes relate as acts on one play frame (setting, playing, testing, breaking, extending it), and that frame conditions how canvas calls in the same sub were read

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-002 Boundary work, declared adapted (Gieryn, T. F. (1983) Boundary-work and the demarcation of science from non-science, American Sociological Review; recalled); 8 third-order themes: T3-015, T3-037, T3-063, T3-075, T3-090, T3-140, T3-184, T3-185. Why: containment by rule, venue and argument are kinds of one practice: a host community drawing the line between its business and the event

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-003 Sensemaking, declared borrowed (Weick, K. E. (1995) Sensemaking in Organizations; recalled); 3 third-order themes: T3-016, T3-018, T3-052. Why: explaining the event, decoding pictures and remarking on neighbours are one interpretive work on a novel object

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-004 Frame bridging, declared adapted (Snow, D. A., Rochford, E. B., Worden, S. K. and Benford, R. D. (1986) Frame alignment processes, micromobilization, and movement participation, American Sociological Review; recalled); 4 third-order themes: T3-031, T3-086, T3-135, T3-179. Why: in-jokes, fandom lore, imported quarrels and ideology read from the canvas are all one move: an existing frame carried onto the episode

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-005 Mobilization, declared adapted (McCarthy, J. D. and Zald, M. N. (1977) Resource mobilization and social movements: a partial theory, American Journal of Sociology; recalled); 5 third-order themes: T3-002, T3-062, T3-104, T3-144, T3-167. Why: calling, recruiting kindred subs, cheering, quiet recruiting and timed placement are kinds of gathering placing time

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-006 Collective representation, declared adapted (Durkheim, E. (1912) Les formes elementaires de la vie religieuse; recalled); 10 third-order themes: T3-004, T3-033, T3-077, T3-082, T3-092, T3-160, T3-169, T3-175, T3-191, T3-197. Why: proposal, design, signature, tribute and adoption of a found mark are kinds of one act: a room choosing the emblem that stands for it

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-007 Stigmergy, declared borrowed (Grasse, P.-P. (1959) La reconstruction du nid et les coordinations inter-individuelles, Insectes Sociaux; Heylighen, F. (2016) Stigmergy as a universal coordination mechanism, Cognitive Systems Research; recalled); 3 third-order themes: T3-038, T3-041, T3-060. Why: building, extending and adding to a shared mark are one coordination through the trace the work leaves

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-008 Standardization of output, declared borrowed (Mintzberg, H. (1979) The Structuring of Organizations; recalled); 5 third-order themes: T3-008, T3-034, T3-049, T3-070, T3-091. Why: circulating, asking for, enforcing and demanding one plan are kinds of coordination by a specified output

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-009 Workarounds, declared adapted (Gasser, L. (1986) The integration of computing and routine work, ACM Transactions on Office Information Systems; recalled); 8 third-order themes: T3-027, T3-028, T3-074, T3-088, T3-089, T3-108, T3-120, T3-168. Why: scripts, extra accounts, timer tricks and the governance of scripts all answer one rule, the rate limit

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move relating (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-010 Backstage decision-making, declared adapted (Goffman, E. (1959) The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life (the back region); recalled); 7 third-order themes: T3-014, T3-107, T3-109, T3-114, T3-116, T3-132, T3-152. Why: the venue themes relate as sides of one move, the split between a closed place of decision and the public thread

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-011 Decided order, declared borrowed (Ahrne, G. and Brunsson, N. (2011) Organization outside organizations: the significance of partial organization, Organization; recalled); 8 third-order themes: T3-066, T3-101, T3-103, T3-121, T3-125, T3-172, T3-173, T3-187. Why: leaders, votes, elections, oaths, sanctions, divisions of work and their stated absence are the decided elements of partial organization

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-012 Collective efficacy, declared borrowed (Bandura, A. (1997) Self-Efficacy: The Exercise of Control; Bandura, A. (2000) Exercise of human agency through collective efficacy, Current Directions in Psychological Science; recalled); 5 third-order themes: T3-036, T3-059, T3-098, T3-136, T3-181. Why: doubt, judging the canvas full, questioning presence, urging surrender and quitting all voice the room's belief in its own capability

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-013 Repair work, declared adapted (Jackson, S. J. (2014) Rethinking repair, in Gillespie, Boczkowski and Foot (eds) Media Technologies; recalled); 6 third-order themes: T3-005, T3-021, T3-042, T3-055, T3-069, T3-141. Why: watching, repairing, defending, night cover, hardening the mark and putting upkeep first are kinds of keeping a work against erosion

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-014 Territoriality, declared borrowed (Brown, G., Lawrence, T. B. and Robinson, S. L. (2005) Territoriality in organizations, Academy of Management Review; recalled); 7 third-order themes: T3-012, T3-020, T3-022, T3-039, T3-045, T3-123, T3-124. Why: choosing, claiming, refusing, yielding, granting and abandoning a spot are kinds of one ownership claim over space

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move relating (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-015 Live and let live, declared borrowed (Axelrod, R. (1984) The Evolution of Cooperation; Ashworth, T. (1980) Trench Warfare 1914-1918: The Live and Let Live System; recalled); 11 third-order themes: T3-007, T3-024, T3-025, T3-040, T3-046, T3-047, T3-076, T3-102, T3-119, T3-139, T3-183. Why: sparing, reining in, appealing, apologising, making up, defying and regretting relate as the moves of a tacit cycle of restraint

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-016 Negotiated order, declared borrowed (Strauss, A. (1978) Negotiations: Varieties, Contexts, Processes and Social Order; Strauss, A. et al. (1963) The hospital and its negotiated order; recalled); 11 third-order themes: T3-010, T3-030, T3-067, T3-083, T3-126, T3-138, T3-149, T3-161, T3-193, T3-194, T3-195. Why: borders, truces, envoys, held and broken agreements and disputes over who speaks for a room are kinds of explicit, renegotiable order between rooms

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move relating (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-017 Reciprocity, declared borrowed (Gouldner, A. W. (1960) The norm of reciprocity: a preliminary statement, American Sociological Review; recalled); 7 third-order themes: T3-011, T3-071, T3-072, T3-084, T3-115, T3-122, T3-151. Why: asking, giving, trading, refusing and thanking for help relate as the sides of one obligation to return it

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-018 Meta-organization, declared borrowed (Ahrne, G. and Brunsson, N. (2008) Meta-Organizations; Ahrne, G. and Brunsson, N. (2005) Organizations and meta-organizations, Scandinavian Journal of Management; recalled); 9 third-order themes: T3-013, T3-019, T3-035, T3-056, T3-094, T3-099, T3-150, T3-153, T3-162. Why: hubs, hosts, approvals, protection, alliances, councils and joint marks are kinds of organization whose members are rooms

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move relating (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-019 Attribution, declared adapted (Heider, F. (1958) The Psychology of Interpersonal Relations; Kelley, H. H. (1967) Attribution theory in social psychology, Nebraska Symposium on Motivation; recalled); 4 third-order themes: T3-087, T3-118, T3-170, T3-188. Why: tracing, exonerating, blaming and disowning relate as inferences that decide the room's response to a change

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-020 Repertoire of contention, declared adapted (Tilly, C. (1978) From Mobilization to Revolution; Tilly, C. (1995) Popular Contention in Great Britain, 1758-1834; recalled); 7 third-order themes: T3-006, T3-061, T3-068, T3-128, T3-176, T3-178, T3-192. Why: erasing, encroaching, converting, raiding, sabotage and harassment are kinds of one learned set of attack performances

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-021 Rivalry, declared borrowed (Kilduff, G. J., Elfenbein, H. A. and Staw, B. M. (2010) The psychology of rivalry: a relationally dependent analysis of competition, Academy of Management Journal; recalled); 5 third-order themes: T3-050, T3-058, T3-134, T3-154, T3-155. Why: taunts, chants, victory claims, salutes and kept grievances are kinds of address to a particular rival

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-022 Flagging the nation, declared adapted (Billig, M. (1995) Banal Nationalism; recalled); 12 third-order themes: T3-065, T3-078, T3-079, T3-081, T3-085, T3-113, T3-130, T3-142, T3-145, T3-165, T3-166, T3-180. Why: the flag, its emblems, kin flags, national history, politics, belonging and national others are kinds of one practice: the nation reproduced through a shared artefact

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-023 Neo-tribes, declared borrowed (Maffesoli, M. (1996) The Time of the Tribes: The Decline of Individualism in Mass Society; recalled); 6 third-order themes: T3-096, T3-137, T3-163, T3-171, T3-174, T3-190. Why: hailing, spreading, defecting to, joining and splitting colour factions are kinds of belonging to a canvas-born aesthetic grouping

Fourth-order theme cut (section 8), move merging (Grodal, Anteby and Holm): T4-024 Symbolic boundaries, declared adapted (Lamont, M. and Molnar, V. (2002) The study of boundaries in the social sciences, Annual Review of Sociology; recalled); 5 third-order themes: T3-080, T3-143, T3-146, T3-177, T3-182. Why: covering hate symbols, shutting down bigotry, judging symbols and jokes, and the calls to transgress are kinds of drawing a moral line on an open surface
